routes.reason: New roadmap LevelOneAutomorphicFormsForClassicalGroups for the level one automorphic forms of split classical groups over Z, the level one algebraic cusp forms of PGL_m that parametrise them, and Siegel modular forms for Sp_2g(Z), with 116 items and a 1069-word brief that states Theorems 1–7 as the paper does and names the imports. The area automorphic is a galaxy id and the id appears in no other extraction. I searched every layer description in data/atlas.json for level one forms and Siegel modular forms: the only hits are the Tau Ceti ModularForms roadmap's SL_2 material and unrelated 'level' terminology in BelyiMaps, so nothing owns this direction and a new roadmap rather than a Part II is right.

Source of AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 for Harish-Chandra's criterion for the existence of discrete series and the archimedean Langlands correspondence for GL_n(R). AF.1 owns the foundations of real reductive representation theory, which is exactly what both are.

Source of AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1 for the ε-factors of representations of W_R in Tate's normalisation. AL.1 fixes local L-, ε- and γ-factors in that normalisation, so the archimedean case belongs there.

Source of AL.3 for Gelbart–Shahidi's boundedness of Λ(s, π × π′) in vertical strips, which completes the analytic package AL.3 owns for Rankin–Selberg L-functions and which the explicit formula consumes.

Source of AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3 for Mestre's formalism and the explicit formula for an L-function with Euler product, functional equation, finitely many poles and bounded vertical growth. AN.3 plans explicit formulas with test-function hypotheses, which is the shape of Proposition 2.2 here.

Source of AN.6 for the (GRH) hypothesis of Section 4.3 used by Theorem 4. AN.6 keeps the register of RH- and GRH-type hypotheses for conditional theorems, so the conditional statement is anchored where the hypothesis lives.

Source of AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.6 for Arthur's L²-Lefschetz formula and its evaluation at pseudocoefficients of discrete series. AS.6 owns Arthur's invariant trace formula, which the paper cites for exactly this.

Source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 for the Adams–Johnson packets being Arthur packets with multiplicity one and for Moeglin–Renard's description. ML.4 gives the Arthur–Mok classification inputs their proof-source owners, packets included.

Source of GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 for the spinor norm over rings with its GSpin and Spin exact sequences, Zassenhaus's formula and the Conway–Sloane mass computations. GN.2 owns quadratic forms over fields and rings with discriminants, Clifford invariants and spinor genera; the extraction's library item cites Tau Ceti's CliffordAlgebra.spinorNorm for the field case, which is consistent with routing only the ring-level statements here.

Source of MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.3 for Rallis's relation between Satake parameters under the unramified theta correspondence, a local statement about theta modules for orthogonal–symplectic dual pairs, which MP.3 owns.

Source of ComputationalNumberTheory CN.4 for the certified evaluation of F̂_ℓ(0), F̂_ℓ(i/4π) and J_{F_ℓ}(U) from digamma values and tail-bounded series. CN.4 owns interval and ball arithmetic and validated evaluation of analytic quantities, which is precisely what Section 2.4.3 does.

Source of CN.5 for the paper's proofs by computation as certificates: the triples (ℓ, S′, t) with their interval checks and the sets Λ of Section 3.3. CN.5 defines certificate schemas and checks certificates, and this paper is an unusually good source for them, since the authors publish the certificate files themselves.

notes: Accept, no corrections needed. The recorded hash of the published open-access PDF reproduces (ea90fb0f…) and I re-extracted all 63 pages, mapping printed pages 261–323 from the running heads. Structure: 151 items (134 missing, 12 planned, 5 library), every missing item routed exactly once, all eleven source stage ids exist, all twelve planned layer ids exist, the new roadmap's area is a galaxy id and its id appears in no other extraction, and check_paper.py passes. All twelve declarations behind the five library items resolve at the pins: Matrix.symplecticGroup, TauCeti.QuadraticMap.specialOrthogonalGroup and orthogonalGroup, NumberField.Embeddings.pow_eq_one_of_norm_eq_one (Kronecker), the three CliffordAlgebra spinor-norm declarations, the two cyclotomic evaluation lemmas and the three Deligne Γ-factor declarations. Locators: 63 of 65 name-and-page checks land on exactly the page given, and the two others are E4's, where Theorem 3 and Proposition 4.1 are stated on p.295 and proved from p.296 on. What makes this extraction unusual is that most of its findings are claims about the authors' published computations, so I checked them against the primary material rather than against the prose: I downloaded the authors' data archive (levelone_src_data.tar.gz from the URL the bibliography gives) and the arXiv TeX, and every one of the eleven findings holds. E4, E5, E6, E7 and E8 are confirmed directly from log_w23_mult1, contradict_vect/db_w23_mult1 and gp/sheet_w23_grh.gp — 12293 elements, 12106 negative and 187 not; the 181 with I_23 twice being exactly the V of Proposition 4.1(2), with dimensions from 10 to 38 rather than the printed 14 to 42; the entry for I_1+I_7+I_13+I_17+I_21+2I_23 carrying the non-negative value +0.036, so that it is not excluded at δ = m = 1 and the worksheet has to eliminate it separately; and the worksheet's own δ = 0, m = 2. E2 and E10 are confirmed from the authors' ex_poids_connus(), whose 26 entries include [[0,0,23], 2] with multiplicity two, which is what makes 27 elements collapse to 26 and 16 elements to 15. E3 is confirmed from the definition of CFnorminit, whose diagonal term Σ v_i²/m_i gives β_Q(ρe_1, ρe_1) = 1 − 2K against β_{Q′}(e_1, e_1) = 1/2 − K, so ρ is an isometry for the Euclidean structures but not for β. E9 follows from the dimension count (odd dimensions up to 15 need Sp_14). E11 is visible in the arXiv TeX, which cites the same tail estimates as '(3) p.127' in one place and '(3) p. 277' in another. E1 I checked by writing my own enumeration: Definition 3.1's classes of degree-14 products of cyclotomic polynomials with X+1 of even multiplicity, modulo P(X) ∼ P(−X), number 1158 — (2257 + 59)/2 — and the same program reproduces every other entry of Table 2, 3, 12, 32, 92, 219, 530 and 2521, so the printed 1157 at Sp_14 is the only wrong one. Nothing was corrected, rejected or deleted, and I add no finding: I read §§1–4 around the findings and the statements the routes cite, not all 63 pages line by line.
